arxiv-2105-01540.title: A Gentle Introduction to Scaling Laws in Biological Systems
arxiv-2105-01540.creator: Fabiano L. Ribeiro 1 * and William R. L. S. Pereira 2 ⋄ \diamond
arxiv-2105-01540.description: Abstract This paper investigates the role of size in biological organisms. More specifically, how the energy demand, expressed by the metabolic rate, changes according to the mass of an organism. Empirical evidence suggests a power-law relation between mass and metabolic rate, namely allometric law.

arxiv-2106-04225.title: On the role of feedback in visual processing: a predictive coding perspective
arxiv-2106-04225.creator: Andrea AlamiaCerCo, CNRS, 31052 Toulouse, France andrea.alamia@cnrs.fr, Milad MozafariCerCo, CNRS, 31052 Toulouse, FranceIRIT, CNRS, 31062, Toulouse, France milad.mozafari@cnrs.fr Bhavin ChoksiCerCo, CNRS, 31052 Toulouse, France bhavin.choksi@cnrs.fr Rufin VanRullenCerCo, CNRS, 31052 Toulouse, Franc
arxiv-2106-04225.description: Abstract Brain-inspired machine learning is gaining increasing consideration, particularly in computer vision. Several studies investigated the inclusion of top-down feedback connections in convolutional networks; however, it remains unclear how and when these connections are functionally helpful. Here we address this question in the context of object recognition under noisy conditions.

arxiv-2204-00215.title: Federated Learning Framework Coping with Hierarchical Heterogeneity in Cooperative ITS
arxiv-2204-00215.creator: Rui Song, Liguo Zhou, Venkatnarayanan Lakshminarasimhan, Andreas Festag, Alois Knoll
arxiv-2204-00215.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Rui Song, Liguo Zhou, Venkatnarayanan Lakshminarasimhan, Andreas Festag, Alois Knoll. Deep learning is a key approach for the environment perception function of Cooperative Intelligent Transportation Systems (C-ITS) with autonomous vehicles and smart traffic infrastructure. The performance of the object recognition and detection strongly depends on the data volume in the model training, which is usually not sufficient due to the limited data collected by a typically small fleet of test vehicles.

arxiv-2303-10854.title: Dynamic Documentation for AI Systems DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX
arxiv-2303-10854.creator: Soham Mehta, Anderson Rogers, Thomas Krendl Gilbert
arxiv-2303-10854.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Soham Mehta, Anderson Rogers, Thomas Krendl Gilbert. AI documentation is a rapidly-growing channel for coordinating the design of AI technologies with policies for transparency and accessibility. Calls to standardize and enact documentation of algorithmic harms and impacts are now commonplace. However, documentation standards for AI remain inchoate, and fail to match the capabilities and social effects of increasingly impactful architectures such as Large Language Models (LLMs).

arxiv-2306-06643.title: Detection and Recovery of Hidden Submatrices
arxiv-2306-06643.creator: Marom Dadon Wasim Huleihel Tamir Bendory
arxiv-2306-06643.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the problems of detection and recovery of hidden submatrices with elevated means inside a large Gaussian random matrix. We consider two different structures for the planted submatrices. In the first model, the planted matrices are disjoint, and their row and column indices can be arbitrary.

arxiv-2402-08071.title: Contagion on Financial Networks: An Introduction
arxiv-2402-08071.creator: Sunday Akukodi Ugwu
arxiv-2402-08071.description: Abstract This mini-project models propagation of shocks, in time point, through links in connected banks. In particular, financial network of 100 banks out of which 15 are shocked to default (that is, 85.00% of the banks are solvent) is modelled using Erdős and Rényi network – directed, weighted and randomly generated network.

arxiv-2405-12314.title: Holographic vacuum energy regularization and corrected entropy of de Sitter space
arxiv-2405-12314.creator: S. Jalalzadeh, H. Moradpour, H. Tebyanian
arxiv-2405-12314.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by S. Jalalzadeh, H. Moradpour, H. Tebyanian. We propose that the spectrum of the surface area of the apparent horizon (AH) of de Sitter (dS) spacetime leads to corrected temperature and entropy of the dS spacetime, offering new insights into its thermodynamic properties. This is done by employing the spectrum of the AH radius, acquired from the Wheeler–DeWitt (WDW) equation, together with the Stefan–Boltzmann law, the time-energy uncertainty relation, and the unified first law of thermodynamics.

arxiv-2410-13751.title: Abundances of iron-peak elements in 58 bulge spheroid stars from APOGEE
arxiv-2410-13751.creator: B. Barbuy and A.C.S. Friaça and H. Ernandes and P. da Silva and S. O. Souza and J. G. Fernández-Trincado and K. Cunha and V. V. Smith and T. Masseron and A. Pérez-Villegas and C. Chiappini and A.B.A. Queiroz and B. X. Santiago and T. C. Beers and F. Anders and R. P. Schiavon and M. Valentini and D.
arxiv-2410-13751.description: Abstract Context. Stars presently identified in the bulge spheroid are probably very old, and their abundances can be interpreted as due to the fast chemical enrichment of the early Galactic bulge. The abundances of the iron-peak elements are important tracers of nucleosynthesis processes, in particular oxygen burning, silicon burning, the weak s s -process, and α \alpha -rich freeze-out. Aims.

arxiv-2501-12441.title: Probing Standard Model and Beyond with Reactor CE ν \nu NS Data of CONUS+ experiment
arxiv-2501-12441.creator: Ayan Chattaraj, Anirban Majumdar, Rahul Srivastava
arxiv-2501-12441.description:
Abstract We explore the potential of reactor antineutrino-induced Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering (CE ν 
u NS) data from the CONUS+ experiment to investigate both the Standard Model (SM) and Beyond Standard Model (BSM) scenarios. Alongside CE ν 
u NS, Elastic Neutrino-Electron Scattering (E ν 
u ES) events are also included in our analysis, enabling more stringent constraints on new physics.

arxiv-2509-00165.title: Strata of Ecological Coexistence via Grassmannians
arxiv-2509-00165.creator: Türkü Özlüm Çelik, Pierre A. Haas, Georgy Scholten, Kexin Wang, Giulio Zucal
arxiv-2509-00165.description: Abstract We study the Lotka–Volterra system from the perspective of computational algebraic geometry, focusing on equilibria that are both feasible and stable. These conditions stratifies the parameter space in ℝ n × ℝ n × n \mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}^{n\times n} with the feasible-stable semialgebraic sets.

arxiv-2509-05243.title: Rethinking mass transfer: a unified semi-analytical framework for circular and eccentric binaries
arxiv-2509-05243.creator: A. Parkosidis, S. Toonen, F. Dosopoulou, E. Laplace
arxiv-2509-05243.description: Abstract Context. Mass transfer (MT) is a fundamental process in stellar evolution. While MT in circular orbits is well studied, observations indicate that it also occurs in eccentric ones. To date, no framework simultaneously accounts for both conservative and non-conservative MT across arbitrary eccentricities while also incorporating the donor star’s spin. Aims.

arxiv-2509-20206.title: Non-overlap Average Treatment Effect Bounds
arxiv-2509-20206.creator: Herbert P. Susmann ∗, Alec McClean ∗, Iván Díaz
arxiv-2509-20206.description: Abstract The average treatment effect (ATE), the mean difference in potential outcomes under treatment and control, is a canonical causal effect. Overlap , which says that all subjects have non-zero probability of either treatment status, is necessary to identify and estimate the ATE.

arxiv-2512-13042.title: A variant of Röhr’s vanishing theorem with an application to the normal reduction number for normal surface singularities Thanks: TO was partially supported by JSPS Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (C) Grant Number 21K03215. KW was partially supported by JSPS Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research
arxiv-2512-13042.creator: Tomohiro Okuma, Kei-ichi Watanabe, Ken-ichi Yoshida
arxiv-2512-13042.description: Abstract . Let A A be an excellent two-dimensional normal local ring containing an algebraically closed field and let X → Spec ⁡ ( A ) X\to\spec(A) be a resolution of singularity. We prove a theorem giving a condition under which the dimension of the cohomology group of invertible sheaves on X X coincides with a natural lower bound.

arxiv-2602-19185.title: Some effective operators for graphene monolayer superlattices, from variational perturbation theory
arxiv-2602-19185.creator: Louis Garrigue
arxiv-2602-19185.description: Abstract . Our goal is to provide precise effective operators for monolayer graphene at Fermi energy. We consider the microscopic potential created by a lattice, and add a macroscopic potential with the same periodicity but varying at a scale ε − 1 ∈ ℕ \varepsilon^{-1}\in\mathbb{N} , creating a superlattice.

arxiv-2603-03550.creator: Zhiyu Cao, Peter G. Wolynes

pmc-10618706.creator: Alessandro Innocenti, Alice Letizia Andreoli
pmc-10618706.description: ridement- necrosectomy, ligation of right and left spermatic cords and local skin flap reconstruction. We congratulate with the Authors for their article, and we completely agree with them for the chosen reconstructive strategy, but we have some elements to discuss. The state of the art shows many different techniques for shaft penile reconstruction, including skin grafts, local and free flaps.

pmc-11598658.title: Incidence of SARS-CoV-2 Infection Among European Healthcare Workers and Effectiveness of the First Booster COVID-19 Vaccine, VEBIS HCW Observational Cohort Study, May 2021–May 2023
pmc-11598658.creator: Camelia Savulescu, Albert Prats-Uribe, Kim Brolin, Zvjezdana Lovrić Makarić, Anneli Uusküla, Georgios Panagiotakopoulos, Colm Bergin, Catherine Fleming, Antonella Agodi, Paolo Bonfanti, Rita Murri, Viesturs Zvirbulis, Dace Zavadska, Konstanty Szuldrzynski, Ausenda Machado, Corneliu Petru Popescu, Mi
pmc-11598658.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: European countries have included healthcare workers (HCWs) among priority groups for COVID-19 vaccination. We established a multi-country hospital network to measure the SARS-CoV-2 incidence and effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines among HCWs against laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. Methods: HCWs from 19 hospitals in 10 countries participated in a dynamic prospective cohort study, providing samples for SARS-CoV-2 testing at enrolment and during weekly/fortnightly follow-up.

pmc-12487449.title: Berberine-based strategies: novel delivery systems bring out new potential for wound healing
pmc-12487449.creator: Jie Yin, Siqi Qin, Junren Chen, Napsan Wong, Cheng Peng, Dan Li
pmc-12487449.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Wound healing is a highly regulated biological process that restores tissue integrity following injury, while it could be disrupted in specific conditions such as diabetes mellitus (DM) and bacterial infection, leading to delayed healing and serious complications. Berberine (BBR) is a pivotal naturally occurring isoquinoline alkaloid with multiple pharmacological activities, especially anti-inflammation, anti-bacteria, anti-oxidative stress, which are beneficial for wound healing.

pmc-12592592.title: An Open‐Label, Multicenter, Phase II Study of Bexarotene in Patients with Adult T‐Cell Leukemia/Lymphoma
pmc-12592592.creator: Kentaro Yonekura, Ikko Muto, Motoi Takenaka, Jun Aoi, Taku Fujimura, Masahiro Amano, Takuro Kanekura, Takuya Miyagi, Kanami Saito, Eiji Kiyohara, Takatoshi Shimauchi, Ken Watanabe, Tomoko Miyake, Takamichi Ito, Hisashi Uhara, Kazuyasu Fujii, Akihito Sudo, Toshiki Watanabe, Keiji Iwatsuki
pmc-12592592.description: A multicenter, open‐label, historically controlled, 2‐arm phase II study was conducted to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of bexarotene in Japanese patients with adult T‐cell lymphoma/leukemia (ATL). The study enrolled patients with indolent ATL and skin lesions and patients with aggressive ATL who had skin relapse after achieving remission following ≥ 1 regimen of systemic chemotherapy.

pmc-12662873.title: New insights into the ectoparasite fauna of bats (Phyllostomidae and Vespertilionidae) in the Baja California Peninsula, Mexico
pmc-12662873.creator: Aimée I. Del Río-Trujillo, Juan B. Morales-Malacara, Aldo A. Guevara-Carrizales, Martín Y. Cabrera-Garrido, F. Sara Ceccarelli, Andrés Martínez-Aquino
pmc-12662873.description: Bat ectoparasites are an integral part of the wildlife and of host-parasite interactions in the Baja California Peninsula (BCP), Mexico, but the study of these ectoparasites is scarce in this area. In this study the ectoparasite faunal composition of the bat families Phyllostomidae and Vespertilionidae was determined and the first ectoparasitic checklist from BCP was developed.

pmc-12667416.title: Exploring Gut Microbe-Host Genes in Postpartum Depression: Mendelian Randomization and Transcriptomic Analysis
pmc-12667416.creator: Ting Cong, Jing Liu, Li Yuan, Zhenchen Chu
pmc-12667416.description: PurposeTo suggest a potential causal role of gut microbiota in Postpartum depression (PPD) and identify susceptible microbiota-host genes.Patients and MethodsThe two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study was carried out with the genome-wide association studies (GWAS) data of 196 gut microbial taxa and PPD. Causal relationships were evaluated with inverse variance weighted (IVW), MR‒Egger, weighted mode, and weighted median approaches.

pmc-13196944.title: The need for balanced dengue vaccine protection: Insights from Thai surveillance data on four serotypes
pmc-13196944.creator: Ruchira R Khosavanna, Sopon Iamsirithaworn, Soontorn Pinpaiboon, Kanyarat Phutthasophit, Taweewun Hunsawong, Albert I Ko, Kathryn B Anderson, Darunee Buddhari, Jonas Klingström, Jonas Klingström, Michael R Holbrook, Jonas Klingström, Michael R Holbrook
pmc-13196944.description: Dengue virus (DENV), comprising four distinct serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4), poses a major public health challenge in tropical regions. Infection with one serotype confers long-term immunity to that serotype alone, while subsequent heterologous infections are associated with increased risk of severe disease, necessitating vaccines that induce durable, balanced immunity across all serotypes.

pmc-13318382.title: A Closed Glottis After Shoulder Arthroscopy: A Rare Airway Complication of Interscalene Block Causing Postoperative Respiratory Failure
pmc-13318382.creator: Gonzalo J Martinez-Ruiz, Nickolle A Cruz-Figueroa, Luis Garcia-Requena, Bak N Choi-Reina, Jose A Torres-Cintron
pmc-13318382.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Interscalene brachial plexus block (ISB) is commonly used for shoulder surgery and is associated with predictable complications such as phrenic nerve palsy due to its proximity to adjacent neural structures. While the spread of local anesthetic may involve the recurrent laryngeal nerve, resulting in vocal cord dysfunction, which is uncommon, progression to bilateral vocal cord paralysis, causing acute airway obstruction, is exceedingly rare.A 74-year-old obese female underwent elective outpatient right shoulder arthroscopy under ultrasound-guided interscalene block with bupivacaine.

pmc-13384615.title: Effect of goal-directed fluid resuscitation therapy based on peripheral perfusion index on acute skin failure in elderly critically ill patients: A randomized controlled trial
pmc-13384615.creator: Bing Xu, Jiuying Ji, Yin Yan, Ling Lu, Zunguo Pu, Peirong Wang, Ying Wang, Yaqing Zhou
pmc-13384615.description: Background:This study aimed to evaluate the effect of the peripheral perfusion index (PPI)-based goal-directed fluid resuscitation strategy for reducing the incidence of acute skin failure (ASF) in elderly critically ill patients.Methods:We conducted a prospective, randomized, parallel-controlled study by enrolling 216 elderly critically ill patients who required early active fluid resuscitation from January 2025 to December 2025.

pmc-13424256.title: Subcutaneous Zygomycosis Successfully Treated With Itraconazole Monotherapy: A Case Report From Central India
pmc-13424256.creator: Saurabh D Kose, Kirtee Meshram, Sushil Pande, Minal Jogi
pmc-13424256.description: Subcutaneous zygomycosis, also known as basidiobolomycosis, is a rare, chronic fungal infection that predominantly affects immunocompetent individuals in tropical and subtropical regions. The disease often presents as firm, painless, indurated subcutaneous swellings that may mimic malignancy, chronic bacterial infections, tuberculosis, or other deep fungal infections, leading to frequent misdiagnosis and unnecessary surgical interventions.

pmc-13429233.title: Evaluating the prognostic value of mutational signatures in small-cell lung cancer through reference-based signature assignment and continuous activity analysis
pmc-13429233.creator: Rishabh Garg, Kira A. Glasmacher, Arnaud Augert, Jeffrey P. Townsend
pmc-13429233.description: BackgroundSmall-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive malignancy with poor survival outcomes. Biomarkers that reliably capture tumor mutational burden (TMB), tumor immunogenicity, and prognosis could substantially improve clinical stratification. Prior studies have suggested that mutational signatures, including single-base substitution (SBS) 4 and 13, may be associated with TMB and survival in SCLC.

pmc-13483039.title: Modulating the interfacial solvation structure to promote hydroxyl migration for alkaline hydrogen oxidation
pmc-13483039.creator: Chenggong Niu, Yulin Zhao, Yuchen Lei, Linyu Chen, Zuyang Luo, Heyang Liu, Tingting Tang, Xiaofeng Shi, Lianhai Zu, Wei Zhao, Xiulin Yang, Rui Cao, Jieshan Qiu, Yongfa Zhu, Bin Wu
pmc-13483039.description: Alkaline hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) kinetics are fundamentally governed by electrode-electrolyte interfacial water structure and hydrogen-bond (H-bond) networks, yet their dynamic regulatory mechanism remains elusive. Here we show that precise modulation of the P coordination environment of Ir-based catalysts effectively enhances alkaline HOR catalytic performance.

uslaw-usc-t50-s3366.description: United States Code, Title 50 (War And National Defense); Chapter 45 (Miscellaneous Intelligence Community Authorities); Subchapter IV (Collection, Analysis, And Sharing Of Intelligence). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
